summary: Assign services python code to application workstream in governance manifest

delivery.outcome: Add services/**/*.py to coordination.workstreams.application.ownedPaths in .governance/manifest.json so the Python service code under services/ (currently services/healing-webhook/*.py) is owned by the application workstream. This remediates GOV-WORKSTREAM-003: code2llm-discovered planfile tickets scoped to services/healing-webhook/app.py (PLF-039 and the Shotgun Surgery payload/proc/outcome siblings) could not be allocated to a workstream because no ownedPaths pattern covered those files. Infrastructure keeps services/**/Dockerfile*, which stays disjoint from the new Python-only glob, so rejectActiveScopeOverlap remains satisfied.
nonGoals: No ownership change for services/**/Dockerfile* or any other infrastructure path
No source, test or behaviour change inside services/ itself
No changes to other workstreams' ownedPaths or to coordination settings other than the application list

architecture.decision: Add the single glob services/**/*.py to the application workstream ownedPaths list in .governance/manifest.json, placed with the other code-root globs after packages/**. The glob matches exactly the four Python modules in services/healing-webhook/ and never matches a Dockerfile, so application and infrastructure ownership of services/ stays disjoint under the gate's pattern_covered_by predicate. .governance/manifest.json is not digest-pinned by .governance/manifest.lock.json (only manifest.base.json is), so no lock refresh is required.
dataChanges: application workstream now owns services/**/*.py; services Python code previously matched no workstream and triggered GOV-WORKSTREAM-003 on ticket allocation
architecture.rollback: Revert the ticket commit; application.ownedPaths returns to the previous six globs and services Python code is unowned again.

commands: python3 -c "import json,sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.governance');from governance_check import pattern_covered_by;m=json.load(open('.governance/manifest.json'));ws=m['coordination']['workstreams'];app=ws['application']['ownedPaths'];inf=ws['infrastructure']['ownedPaths'];assert 'services/**/*.py' in app;assert any(pattern_covered_by(p, 'services/**/*.py') for p in ['services/healing-webhook/app.py','services/healing-webhook/app_bootstrap.py','services/healing-webhook/app_command_routing.py','services/healing-webhook/ticket_builder.py']);assert all(not any(pattern_covered_by(p, o) for o in inf) for p in ['services/healing-webhook/app.py']);assert any(pattern_covered_by('services/healing-webhook/Dockerfile', o) for o in inf) and not any(pattern_covered_by('services/healing-webhook/Dockerfile', o) for o in app)"
validation.evidence: The gate ownership predicate resolves every services/healing-webhook/*.py file to application only, keeps services Dockerfiles with infrastructure only, and the new glob is present in application.ownedPaths.
The governance gate reports 0 errors from the ticket worktree.
